hf: Top model repository’s downloads over the previous 30 days, checked Nov 18. For small-model leaderboard publishers, the linked submission is used.
gh: Lifetime stars on the relevant linked project or the most-starred public, non-fork repo of the listed organization. Includes tools as well as models.
requests: Mean daily share of Vercel AI Gateway requests, Nov 11–17. The average gives each day equal weight.
spend: Mean daily share of spending on Vercel AI Gateway, Nov 11–17. The average gives each day equal weight.
tokens: Mean daily share of Vercel AI Gateway tokens, Nov 11–17. The average gives each day equal weight.
imageCount: Mean daily share of Vercel AI Gateway images generated, Nov 11–17. The average gives each day equal weight.
videoCount: Mean daily share of Vercel AI Gateway videos generated, Nov 11–17. The average gives each day equal weight.

labs.name: 0arch.io
labs.focus: Published Kisoku, an open base-model experiment.

team.background: Pretrained and tested Kisoku 1.6B as an individual research project.

innovation.assessment: Documents pretraining and extension to 64K context. It demonstrates individual-scale training under constrained resources. Benchmark parity is mixed and limited to the reported comparisons.

labs.name: Aaru
labs.focus: Builds simulated populations for testing products, messages, and policies.

people.names: Cameron Fink, Ned Koh, John Kessler

innovation.assessment: Provides a working research product for comparing scenarios. The public product material establishes an application. Predictive accuracy depends on validation for the particular population and setting.

labs.name: AGI Inc
labs.focus: Builds action models and software for on-device computer use.

people.names: Div Garg, Steve Frey, Naman Garg

innovation.assessment: The company reports building its own action models and testing them on device-control tasks. The public evidence is specialized to reported benchmarks and operating conditions.

labs.name: Answer.AI
labs.focus: Co-developed ModernBERT, an encoder architecture for longer context and efficient retrieval.

innovation.example: ModernBERT, joint work with LightOn and collaborators
innovation.assessment: Brings current attention and training techniques to an encoder with native 8,192-token context. The paper measures retrieval and classification. Credit is shared by the project team.
innovation.note: ModernBERT encodes a document into representations that another system can use for search or classification. The team and collaborators revisited both the encoder architecture and how much data to train it on.

labs.name: Applied Compute
labs.focus: Provides model training and inference infrastructure and runs customer-specific post-training.

people.names: Yash Patil, Rhythm Garg, Linden Li

innovation.assessment: The company describes custom training for customers and an open-model platform. Its public material supports applied training work. A general architecture advance is outside those examples.

labs.name: Arcee AI
labs.focus: Trains open foundation models, including the Trinity mixture-of-experts family.

people.names: Mark McQuade, Jacob Solawetz, Brian Benedict

innovation.assessment: Adds independently trained open checkpoints. MoE routing has prior art. The demonstrable contribution is the resulting model and training work under the released configuration.

labs.name: Arda
labs.focus: Builds software for industrial engineering and manufacturing workflows.

people.names: Bob McGrew, Augustus Odena, Alex Mark, Jakob Frick

innovation.assessment: The public site describes tools that organize work such as design, process planning, and production. It leaves a separately attributable model or training result unestablished.

labs.name: Axiom Math
labs.focus: Develops models that generate and verify formal mathematical proofs in Lean.

innovation.assessment: The value is producing proof artifacts a proof assistant can check. Formal verification establishes whether each proof is valid. It does not by itself establish reproducible success rates or novelty of all results.

labs.name: Basecamp Research
labs.focus: Develops foundation models for therapeutic research.

innovation.assessment: The public model announcement identifies an original research artifact and direction. Clinical impact remains a separate question that requires evidence from specific studies.

labs.name: Bioptimus
labs.focus: Develops the H-Optimus foundation model family for histopathology.

innovation.assessment: Pretrained pathology image representations transfer to a range of research tasks. The public checkpoints and evaluations are the contribution. Clinical utility needs evaluation in the intended setting.

labs.name: Cartesia
labs.focus: Develops low-latency speech models and researches state-space architectures.

people.names: Karan Goel, Albert Gu, Arjun Desai, Brandon Yang

innovation.assessment: A working low-latency product built around state-space model expertise. The team's contribution is the speech system and measured latency under stated conditions. State-space sequence models predate Sonic.

labs.name: Causal Labs
labs.focus: Develops physics models for forecasting, starting with weather.

innovation.example: Physics models starting with weather forecasting
innovation.assessment: The stated goal is a reusable model of physical systems. The initial announcement does not establish forecast skill beyond operational baselines or transfer to other domains.

labs.name: Chai Discovery
labs.focus: Developed Chai-1 for molecular structure prediction.

people.names: Joshua Meier, Jack Dent, Matthew McPartlon, Jacques Boitreaud

innovation.assessment: Reports a unified model and comparisons on structure prediction. The gain is scoped to the evaluations reported. The model's existence alone does not establish downstream drug-discovery impact.

labs.name: Core Automation
labs.focus: Researches alternatives to large-scale pretraining and Transformer architectures.

team.background: Team members previously led reinforcement-learning research at OpenAI and pretraining for Gemini.

people.names: Jerry Tworek, Rohan Anil, Joanne Jang, Anmol Gulati, Julia Villagra

innovation.assessment: Reports training a sparse mixture-of-experts model across geographically separated GPU clusters. The contribution is cross-site scheduling and communication engineering. It does not establish a new general-purpose backbone.

labs.name: Corma
labs.focus: Trains models for defensive cybersecurity workflows.

innovation.assessment: The public description covers its modeling and deployment goals. It leaves the contribution beyond established defensive baselines open.

labs.name: CuspAI
labs.focus: Builds AI tools and research partnerships for materials discovery.

innovation.assessment: Brings industrial materials researchers into a shared discovery program. The announcement describes the collaborations and workflow. Model-level novelty needs technical comparisons.

labs.name: Decart
labs.focus: Develops Oasis, an interactive world model trained to generate environments in response to user actions.

people.names: Dean Leitersdorf, Moshe Shalev, Orian Leitersdorf

innovation.assessment: Co-developed with Etched. Demonstrates real-time video conditioned on player input in a constrained world. Prior work includes GameNGen, so the contribution is the particular open implementation and interactive modeling tradeoff.

labs.name: Deep Cogito
labs.focus: Trains models using iterated distillation and amplification.

innovation.assessment: Provides a training signal for intermediate reasoning alongside final answers. Reported gains support the approach on selected models, with the effect sensitive to training and baseline choices.

labs.name: Dream Labs
labs.focus: Trains robot policies for transfer across hardware and tasks.

innovation.assessment: The lab reports testing a trained policy on robot hardware absent from the training set. The report gives a concrete cross-embodiment result. The evidence is specific to the reported tasks and setups.

labs.name: Dyna Robotics
labs.focus: Develops generalist robot foundation models and studies autonomous improvement.

innovation.assessment: The report trains variants on 1,000 to one million hours of human video and tests transfer on held-out robot data. This is evidence for scaling in that setup. General robot reliability still requires deployment tests.

labs.name: Eka Robotics
labs.focus: Develops robot models and hardware that use force feedback during manipulation.

innovation.assessment: The model uses force together with visual observations to handle tasks where contact matters. The examples show an integrated system. They leave the contribution of force sensing and training design to matched evaluations.

labs.name: EleutherAI
labs.focus: Researches language-model training and released the Pythia model suite for studying training dynamics.

innovation.example: Pythia checkpoints across sizes and training steps
innovation.assessment: A deliberately controlled suite lets researchers compare how related models change during training. The innovation is the experimental design and released evidence, not a new architecture.
innovation.note: Pythia released snapshots from many points during training, across models of different sizes. Researchers can compare when a behavior appears and whether larger models learn it sooner.

labs.name: EquiLibre Technologies
labs.focus: Trains reinforcement-learning trading models using experience from game-playing AI.

team.people: Martin Schmid, Matej Moravcik, Rudolf Kadlec
team.background: All three founders worked at DeepMind and IBM. Their publications include DeepStack and Player of Games.

people.names: Martin Schmid, Matej Moravcik, Rudolf Kadlec

innovation.assessment: Applying self-play and game-theory experience to live trading is a concrete deployment. The public evidence does not isolate the model's advantage or establish returns.
innovation.note: The team works on decisions under uncertainty, drawing on reinforcement learning and game theory. The public material gives a research direction and use case while leaving the trading model's implementation private.

labs.name: Essential AI
labs.focus: Trains open language models and publishes research on data and model development.

innovation.assessment: Expands access to independently trained models and related experimental materials. A clean ablation or independently reproduced improvement would be needed to credit a new training method.

labs.name: Fish Audio
labs.focus: Develops multilingual speech generation models and releases model weights.

innovation.example: Fish Audio S2 expressive multilingual speech
innovation.assessment: Released models expose fine-grained delivery control. Expressive TTS predates S2. The practical contribution is supporting controllable multilingual generation in a downloadable release.

labs.name: Flapping Airplanes
labs.focus: Researches data-efficient pretraining and GPU kernels for model training.

team.people: Ben Spector, Asher Spector, Aidan Smith
team.background: The team works across GPU kernels, pretraining, post-training, and inference.

people.names: Ben Spector, Asher Spector, Aidan Smith

innovation.example: Data-efficient model training and GPU megakernels
innovation.assessment: Reports kernel work spanning training and inference. The broader data-efficiency claim needs published model or matched-compute comparisons to quantify the gain.
innovation.note: The question is how to get more learning from the same training data. The public GPU kernel work addresses a related engineering problem by combining multiple operations so GPUs can spend more time doing useful computation.

labs.name: Flourish
labs.focus: Reportedly researches brain-inspired approaches to more energy-efficient AI.

innovation.assessment: Public reporting establishes a research direction. It leaves the design details, measured energy costs, and model results unresolved.

labs.name: Fractale
labs.focus: Trained a 350M language model in an experiment on learned memory.

innovation.assessment: Releases weights and a small-scale memory experiment. An ablation separating learned memory effects from data and model size would strengthen the novelty claim.

labs.name: Fundamental
labs.focus: Pretrained NEXUS to learn from tabular data across different domains.

mentions.title: Fundamental nomination
mentions.author: TheRealDanSaedi
mentions.note: A reply arguing for Fundamental. The live list already carries the company.

innovation.assessment: Pushes large-scale pretraining for enterprise prediction on tables. Tabular foundation models already exist, so the open question is the gain across unseen tasks under matched evaluation.

labs.name: Generalist AI
labs.focus: Develops robot foundation models using data that combine multiple senses.

people.names: Pete Florence, Andy Zeng, Andrew Barry

innovation.assessment: Demonstrates sensor-rich robot learning across manipulation tasks. The contribution is the collected data and trained policy. The effect of each sensor needs matched controls.

labs.name: Genesis AI
labs.focus: Develops a robot foundation model for dexterous manipulation, using both human and robot data.

innovation.assessment: Combines human and robot data to train dexterous behavior. Demos establish a working capability on selected tasks. Unseen-task reliability and the gain from each data source are less clear.

labs.name: Genmo
labs.focus: Trained Mochi, an open video generation model with an asymmetric diffusion Transformer.

innovation.assessment: Allocates model capacity differently to video and text in an open video generator. Its code and weights make the design testable against prior diffusion systems.

labs.name: Goodfire
labs.focus: Tests whether training against internal model representations can shape behavior.

people.names: Eric Ho, Daniel Balsam, Tom McGrath

innovation.assessment: Uses internal representations as a training target and measures the resulting behavior. This differs from judging output alone. The experiments demonstrate targeted effects, with generalization beyond them still uncertain.
innovation.note: The team looks for patterns inside a model that correspond to a behavior. It tests whether making those patterns more or less active during training changes how the model behaves later.

labs.name: Gradium
labs.focus: Develops speech models for real-time voice applications and on-device use.

people.names: Neil Zeghidour, Olivier Teboul, Laurent Mazaré, Alexandre Défossez

innovation.assessment: The Phonon release makes speech models available for local execution. The concrete contribution is the released models and intended deployment setting. Performance depends on device and workload.

labs.name: Guide Labs
labs.focus: Develops the Steerable model family and experiments with architectures for interpretability.

innovation.assessment: Builds interpretable concept representations into a language model and exposes them for inspection and intervention. This makes some controls first-class. It does not make every internal computation or concept transparent.

labs.name: H Company
labs.focus: Develops Holo models for visual grounding and cross-platform computer use.

people.names: Charles Kantor, Laurent Sifre, Karl Tuyls, Daan Wierstra, Julien Perolat

innovation.example: Holo2 desktop and mobile computer-use models
innovation.assessment: Combines grounding and action across several interfaces. Its model release and evaluations support a specialized improvement, with results tied to the reported tasks and compute budgets.

labs.name: Hark
labs.focus: Develops personal AI software and post-trains computer-use models for Handoff.

innovation.assessment: Handoff is a working product and Hark describes post-training alongside software development. The preview leaves the isolated contribution of training and the agent harness open.

labs.name: Harmonic
labs.focus: Trains Aristotle for formal mathematical reasoning and proof search.

innovation.example: Aristotle formal reasoning and proof search
innovation.assessment: Connects a model to machine-checked proofs. Formal checking verifies the output for individual statements. General research ability requires separate task-level comparisons.

labs.name: HiDream.ai
labs.focus: Develops open image generation models, including the HiDream-I1 architecture.

innovation.assessment: Combines a diffusion Transformer with multiple text representations. The released architecture is inspectable. Image benchmark differences do not isolate the contribution of each component.

labs.name: Imbue
labs.focus: Now develops coding-agent tools and previously reported training a 70B language model from scratch.

innovation.assessment: The published work documents a completed model training run and releases training and evaluation tools. It supplies an inspectable research contribution from an earlier phase of the company.

labs.name: Inception Labs
labs.focus: Develops Mercury, a family of diffusion language models.

mentions.title: Inception Labs nomination
mentions.author: sarahcat21
mentions.note: A reply to the early crowdsourced list naming Inception Labs.

people.names: Stefano Ermon, Aditya Grover, Volodymyr Kuleshov

innovation.assessment: Parallel denoising offers a different speed–quality tradeoff from token-by-token generation. Text diffusion predates Mercury. The contribution is making it work in a released model family at larger scale.

labs.name: Ineffable Intelligence
labs.focus: Researches reinforcement-learning systems that learn from experience.

team.background: Silver is a UCL professor and formerly led reinforcement learning at Google DeepMind.

innovation.assessment: The founder sets out a concrete reinforcement-learning agenda. The cited public material offers no model, result, or comparison from which to assign technical credit.
innovation.note: The research agenda asks whether an agent can discover new skills by acting and learning from the consequences. In reinforcement learning, those consequences supply rewards that help it decide which actions to repeat.

labs.name: Intelligent Machines
labs.focus: Reportedly develops robots for complex industrial work.

innovation.assessment: Press reporting describes prototypes and the team’s direction. Public evidence is too limited for a model-level comparison.

labs.name: Isara Labs
labs.focus: Builds systems for modeling decisions with many simulated agents.

innovation.assessment: The public evidence describes the system and its use cases. Controlled comparisons would help establish a specific forecasting or modeling gain.

labs.name: Isomorphic Labs
labs.focus: Co-developed AlphaFold 3 for molecular structure prediction in drug research.

innovation.example: AlphaFold 3, joint work with Google DeepMind
innovation.assessment: Expands structure prediction across multiple molecule classes relative to previous AlphaFold systems. The paper reports comparative gains. Credit belongs to both teams.

labs.name: Kohaku Lab
labs.focus: Develops diffusion models and experiments with efficient diffusion training.

team.background: An open research group publishing diffusion models and tools.

innovation.example: Open diffusion experiments and training tools
innovation.assessment: Publishes training and model work that others can inspect. Public project reports do not establish a consistent advantage over matching open diffusion baselines.

labs.name: Kronos
labs.focus: Published a pretrained model for financial time series and a tokenizer for market data.

innovation.example: Tokenizer and model tailored to financial price and volume data
innovation.assessment: The authors report a 93% relative RankIC gain over their strongest generic time-series foundation model baseline. The result applies to their benchmark, with no demonstrated trading edge.
innovation.note: Financial data arrives as numbers such as price and volume. Kronos learns to turn those records into tokens, then trains a model to predict how the sequence might continue.

labs.name: Kyutai
labs.focus: Developed Moshi, a full-duplex spoken dialogue model.

innovation.example: Moshi full-duplex speech with the Mimi codec
innovation.assessment: Models overlapping speech streams instead of imposing fixed turns. Kyutai reports about 200 ms practical latency on an L4 GPU. Latency alone does not measure turn-taking quality.
innovation.note: Most speech assistants wait for the speaker to finish before producing audio. Moshi processes the incoming and outgoing audio streams together, allowing interruptions and overlap during a conversation.

labs.name: Levanto Labs
labs.focus: Develops Sage, a decision model for closed-ended questions about text and images.

innovation.assessment: Makes categorical decisions directly accessible through a specialized interface. Vendor benchmark results show the targeted task fit. Independent coverage outside those cases remains limited.

labs.name: Lila Sciences
labs.focus: Develops AI systems that work with automated scientific laboratories.

people.names: Geoffrey von Maltzahn, Molly Gibson, Noubar Afeyan, Rafael Gómez-Bombarelli

innovation.assessment: The company documents an integrated loop for scientific analysis, experimentation, and feedback. The showcased workflow establishes an application. Broader model advantages depend on comparable evaluations.

labs.name: Liquid AI
labs.focus: Tests hardware-aware architectures with LFM2, a family of hybrid foundation models.

people.names: Ramin Hasani, Mathias Lechner, Alexander Amini, Daniela Rus

innovation.assessment: Mixes gated short convolutions with attention selected under edge hardware constraints. The report finds up to 2× faster CPU prefill and decoding versus similarly sized models in its tests.
innovation.note: LFM2 mixes attention layers with cheaper operations that work over short stretches of text. The team studies how this mix changes quality and speed on the hardware that will actually run the model.

labs.name: Luma AI
labs.focus: Trains video and image models and deploys them through creative products.

people.names: Amit Jain, Alex Yu, Alberto Taiuti

innovation.assessment: Ray3 is a shipped model with a creative workflow for video generation. The launch demonstrates product and model integration. It leaves the marginal contribution of the reasoning component open.

labs.name: Lvmin Zhang
labs.focus: Published FramePack, a frame-packing method for long video generation.

team.background: Researcher-led, with academic collaborators.

innovation.assessment: Compresses older frames to keep generation context manageable as video length grows. The code and examples demonstrate the engineering tradeoff, without guaranteeing long-range scene consistency.
innovation.note: FramePack is designed to keep video generation from getting progressively more expensive as the clip grows. It summarizes earlier frames so the generator can use their context without retaining every frame at full detail.

labs.name: Magic
labs.focus: Trained LTM-2-mini and researched efficient access to a 100-million-token context.

innovation.assessment: Reports operating on 100M-token inputs with lower memory costs than dense attention in its setup. Advertised context length and reliable recall on arbitrary long tasks are different outcomes.

labs.name: Mantic
labs.focus: Studies training and inference methods for forecasting real-world events.

team.background: The team includes researchers and engineers with backgrounds at Google DeepMind and Palantir.

innovation.assessment: The authors tested a specialized predictor on unseen forecasting questions and report an advantage from post-training over the base model. The result concerns forecasting accuracy, not financial returns.

labs.name: Maritaca AI
labs.focus: Develops Portuguese language models in the Sabiá family and documents language-specific training.

innovation.assessment: Documents gains on Brazilian Portuguese tasks and evaluations. Domain data and evaluation are the distinctive contributions. The report does not establish a generally stronger architecture.

labs.name: Mind Robotics
labs.focus: Develops industrial robots and trains foundation models with manufacturing data.

innovation.assessment: Mind describes collecting data with a manufacturing partner and training models on production tasks. This documents a deployment and learning loop. Transfer to other factories remains a separate result.

labs.name: Mnemonic Labs
labs.focus: Trains a foundation model directly on financial market activity.

team.background: Both founders studied at MIT. Videh did quant research at Citadel and Walleye. Kalki worked at Tower Research Capital.

innovation.example: Training run for a market-native foundation model
innovation.assessment: The launch confirms training is underway. It does not disclose results against a simple market baseline or held-out performance.
innovation.note: The stated aim is to learn from trading activity itself. The public launch describes the training direction and provides too little detail to assess the architecture or how the model performs on future market data.

labs.name: ModelBest
labs.focus: Co-develops the MiniCPM family and researches efficient language and vision models.

innovation.example: MiniCPM family for efficient device-side inference
innovation.assessment: Demonstrates model efficiency and multimodal capability in released checkpoints. These are joint OpenBMB releases. Parameter efficiency and end-to-end device latency are distinct comparisons.

labs.name: nanochat
labs.focus: Trains reference chat models and documents pretraining and post-training end to end.

team.background: Individual-led project with community contributors.

innovation.assessment: Open training, evaluation, and a commit-linked speedrun record make incremental changes comparable. GPT-2-grade means the project’s benchmark threshold, not parity with GPT-2 across all tasks.

labs.name: Nof1
labs.focus: Develops market intelligence models and training environments for financial markets.

team.background: Its team includes alumni of DeepMind, Two Sigma, Citadel, and Bridgewater.

innovation.assessment: Alpha Arena provides a common setting to compare models making market decisions. Performance by third-party models gives no evidence of Nof1's own model advantage.

labs.name: Nomic AI
labs.focus: Trains open embedding models for multimodal and text retrieval.

innovation.assessment: Releases a reproducible long-context text embedder and reports comparisons with proprietary embedding models. The main gain is the combination of context, access, and published training details.
innovation.note: An embedding turns a passage into a vector that search systems can compare by meaning. A longer input window lets this model encode larger passages in one pass.

labs.name: Nous Research
labs.focus: Develops distributed training methods and experiments with open reasoning models.

people.names: Jeffrey Quesnelle, Karan Malhotra, Teknium, Shivani Mitra

innovation.assessment: Investigates optimizers that reduce communication during distributed updates. This is a different systems tradeoff for slow connections. Results at one model scale do not imply unrestricted scaling.

labs.name: Occiglot
labs.focus: Studies continued pretraining and data mixtures for multilingual language models.

innovation.assessment: Adapts a base model to several European languages with published checkpoints. It adds language coverage and a comparison point for multilingual data mixes.

labs.name: Odyssey
labs.focus: Develops interactive world models that generate video in response to actions.

innovation.assessment: Shows generated scenes responding to input over time. The contribution is a working interactive model. Visual coherence is distinct from physically accurate behavior.

labs.name: Overworld
labs.focus: Develops real-time interactive world models for games, including an open release.

innovation.example: Interactive models for generating game environments
innovation.assessment: Gives researchers working action-conditioned generation. The useful evidence is runtime interaction and the release. It leaves long-horizon world consistency and performance against matched models open.

labs.name: Pathway
labs.focus: Proposed and tested the Dragon Hatchling recurrent architecture for language models.

people.names: Zuzanna Stamirowska, Jan Chorowski, Adrian Kosowski

innovation.assessment: Proposes a recurrent language model using a local interaction mechanism and shares reference code. The published work supports architectural novelty at experiment scale. Performance at large deployment scale remains open.
innovation.note: Dragon Hatchling uses a recurrent design. The model carries a state forward as it reads, so earlier inputs can affect later outputs through that state.

labs.name: Periodic Labs
labs.focus: Trains models on physical-science experiment data. Its Neon model analyzes lab results.

team.background: The founding team includes contributors to ChatGPT, OpenAI Operator, and DeepMind’s GNoME and MatterGen.

innovation.example: Periodic Neon analyzes X-ray diffraction data
innovation.assessment: Uses experiment measurements as training data and applies a model inside an operating lab. The public example establishes a narrow analysis workflow. Scientific discovery gains beyond that workflow need separate evidence.

labs.name: Physical Intelligence
labs.focus: Develops generalist robot policies that combine vision, language, and motor actions.

people.names: Sergey Levine, Karol Hausman, Lachy Groom

innovation.assessment: Combines a pretrained vision–language model with a flow-matching action component. Tests reuse across robot bodies and manipulation tasks. Robustness across unseen real environments remains task-dependent.

labs.name: Physical Superintelligence
labs.focus: Builds automated research systems for physics and engineering.

people.names: Matt Pines, Alex Wissner-Gross, Alex Klokus; Alessandro Morari

innovation.assessment: PSI reports that its research system found a proof using an Anthropic model. The public result supports the research system’s contribution. Credit for the underlying model belongs to Anthropic.

labs.name: Pleias
labs.focus: Pretrains language models with openly licensed data and experiments with small reasoning models.

innovation.assessment: Combines a small reasoning model with openly licensed training material. The differentiator is reproducibility and data provenance. Public evaluation does not separate each ingredient's effect.

labs.name: Pluralis Research
labs.focus: Researches decentralized training under low-bandwidth constraints and releases experimental models.

innovation.assessment: Experiments with how to divide model training across weakly connected workers. The value is an alternative systems design. Its cost and coordination benefits depend on the network and workload.

labs.name: Poetiq
labs.focus: Develops a reasoning system that searches and refines solutions using existing language models.

team.background: The founders previously worked at Google and DeepMind.

innovation.assessment: Reported semi-private results test the system’s approach to improving reasoning cost and accuracy. The contribution is in search and orchestration with existing models, whose capabilities also matter.
innovation.note: The system proposes candidate programs for a grid puzzle and tests them against the examples it has been shown. It then revises the candidates before choosing one for the held-out puzzle.

labs.name: Poolside
labs.focus: Trains Laguna coding models and studies reinforcement learning in software-engineering environments.

innovation.assessment: Trains coding models using reinforcement learning in software-engineering environments and releases XS.2 weights. Results establish a competitive coding model in the reported benchmark suite. They do not isolate the training environment's marginal gain.

labs.name: Prime Intellect
labs.focus: Develops distributed training and reinforcement-learning methods, including the INTELLECT models.

innovation.example: INTELLECT-2 distributed RL training of a 32B model
innovation.assessment: Demonstrates reinforcement learning with geographically distributed rollout generation. It extends prior distributed training work. The result does not settle efficiency versus an equivalent centralized run.

labs.name: Project Prometheus
labs.focus: Reportedly builds AI for engineering, manufacturing, and physical systems.

innovation.assessment: The reported scope covers engineering and manufacturing. The public profile leaves the technical result attributable to the parent lab unresolved.

labs.name: QFI Labs
labs.focus: Trains financial language models on disclosures, news, and research.

innovation.assessment: The stated focus is pretraining on financial documents. A verified model result or fair comparison with a general text model is still missing.

labs.name: QSI Labs
labs.focus: Researches financial world models and trains trading agents in market-specific environments.

innovation.example: Research program for market models and RL agents
innovation.assessment: The public description covers several directions. It does not establish a reproducible improvement over a baseline for a named model.

labs.name: Reflection AI
labs.focus: Trained Beam, a sparse mixture-of-experts model, and studied how to control reasoning length during reinforcement learning.

innovation.assessment: The training report tracks the effect of penalizing reasoning length during RL. The contribution is a measured capability–cost tradeoff within Beam, building on earlier mixture-of-experts and RL methods.
innovation.note: A model can spend more computation by writing a longer reasoning trace. Beam’s training experiments probe how explicitly making long traces costly affects answer quality and compute use.

labs.name: Reka AI
labs.focus: Trained the multimodal Core, Flash, and Edge model series with different deployment tradeoffs.

people.names: Dani Yogatama, Cyprien de Masson d'Autume, Yi Tay, Qi Liu

innovation.assessment: Trains broad multimodal models across several size tiers. The contribution is combined modality support and deployable size choices reported in the same research series.

labs.name: Rhoda AI
labs.focus: Trains robot policies using video and robot action data.

innovation.assessment: Rhoda reports extending its Direct Video-Action model to combine mobility and manipulation. The published example tests adaptation with limited additional robot data in selected tasks.
innovation.note: The lab studies whether video can teach robots what an action should accomplish. Its published demonstrations use video prediction together with robot actions to move and manipulate objects in selected tasks.

labs.name: Ricursive Intelligence
labs.focus: Develops AI for chip design and trained its own open-weight language model.

innovation.assessment: Reports training Ripple from scratch and releasing weights for inspection. Its coding results are reported model comparisons. They leave any downstream improvement in chip design to separate evidence.
innovation.note: Ripple-65B combines a dense language model with an explicitly long input window. Ricursive tested whether that design can handle coding tasks competitively and released a checkpoint for others to inspect.

labs.name: RODIN
labs.focus: Pretrained an open one-billion-parameter base model for French.
labs.size: Model card reports a single developer.

innovation.assessment: A from-scratch base model makes French-focused pretraining inspectable. Its main addition is language coverage and a usable checkpoint.

labs.name: RWKV
labs.focus: Develops recurrent language model architectures and publishes trained checkpoints.
labs.size: Started by Bo Peng. Now a broader project.

innovation.assessment: Uses a fixed-size recurrent state for inference with parallelizable training. This changes the memory scaling tradeoff. Its long-context quality still depends on the checkpoint and task.

labs.name: Sakana AI
labs.focus: Experiments with architectures and learning systems, including the Continuous Thought Machine.

team.people: David Ha, Ren Ito, Llion Jones
team.background: Ha led Google Brain’s Tokyo research team. Jones co-authored the Transformer paper.

people.names: David Ha, Ren Ito, Llion Jones

innovation.assessment: Uses neuron synchronization across internal processing steps as a representation. Maze experiments show a working mechanism. They do not establish superiority at language-model scale.
innovation.note: The Continuous Thought Machine gives the network an internal sequence of steps before it answers. It uses the timing of activity across units as information the next stage can read.

labs.name: Sapient Intelligence
labs.focus: Developed a hierarchical recurrent architecture for reasoning, with published weights and experiments.

innovation.assessment: The recurrent design is inspectable. ARC Prize found that repeated refinement and parts of the evaluation setup drove much of the result, limiting credit attributable to the hierarchy itself.
innovation.note: The Hierarchical Reasoning Model updates two recurrent components at different speeds. The slower component maintains a higher-level state as the faster one iterates on the current input.

labs.name: Sarvam AI
labs.focus: Open-sourced 30B and 105B models trained for Indic languages and general reasoning.

innovation.assessment: Releases separately trained models and evaluates Indic-language coverage. The visible advance is language coverage and open access at that scale. Architectural novelty is not the main claim.

labs.name: Scaled Cognition
labs.focus: Trains the APT model family for customer-service agents and tool use.

innovation.assessment: The launch describes training for agentic workflows and comparisons on τ-bench. The result supports a specialized model and workload. It leaves architecture-level advantages across other tasks open.

labs.name: Sesame
labs.focus: Developed CSM for speech generation using conversation context.

innovation.assessment: Conditions speech on conversational context. The public checkpoint demonstrates contextual delivery. End-to-end conversation timing and agent quality depend on the surrounding system.

labs.name: Simile
labs.focus: Trains behavioral simulations and publishes comparisons with survey outcomes.

people.names: Joon Sung Park, Michael Bernstein, Percy Liang, Lainie Yallen

innovation.assessment: The company publishes examples comparing simulations with observed results. The value is a way to test a specific population or question. Generalization depends on population and matching conditions.

labs.name: Skild AI
labs.focus: Trains robot foundation models that adapt across tasks and hardware.

innovation.example: S1 learns a manipulation task in context from one video
innovation.assessment: Compares demonstration conditioning with language prompts on matched training subsets. The report shows stronger transfer on its unseen tasks. Real deployments still depend on the task and environment.

labs.name: Sooth Labs
labs.focus: Researches probabilistic models for forecasting real-world events.

people.names: Chuck Hoover, Yaser Sheikh, Ruslan Salakhutdinov, David LaRose, Shih-En Wei

innovation.assessment: The public statement sets out a forecasting objective. It provides too little evidence to estimate calibration or gains against simple baselines.

labs.name: SpAItial
labs.focus: Develops spatial world models for generating persistent 3D environments.

people.names: Matthias Niessner, Luke Rogers, Ricardo Martin-Brualla, David Novotny

innovation.assessment: The demonstration makes generated scenes usable from more than one viewpoint. Public examples establish a capability in selected scenes. They do not quantify consistency across general scenes.

labs.name: Standard Intelligence
labs.focus: Pretrains computer-use models on video, and develops speech generation models.

team.background: The lab builds models for computer use from video, and publishes work on conversational speech.

innovation.assessment: Uses video-led pretraining for low-level computer actions instead of relying only on a language interface. The demos establish the approach. General task reliability remains less clear.

labs.name: StentorLabs
labs.focus: Experiments with small-model pretraining on free compute, documented in the Portimbria project.
labs.size: Project writeup identifies a solo developer.

team.background: Pretrained and studied Portimbria using free compute.

innovation.assessment: An inspectable small-scale training run shows what a solo researcher can build on free infrastructure. It also documents scale and context changes without isolating which choice improved quality.

labs.name: stmonty (lePokeRed)
labs.focus: Trained a small world model to recreate game dynamics from gameplay.

team.background: Individual publisher.

innovation.example: Small world model trained on Pokémon Red gameplay
innovation.assessment: Shows a compact model reproducing game observations. Its contribution is an accessible experiment in a fixed environment. Transfer to other games is undemonstrated.

labs.name: Subquadratic
labs.focus: Trains language models with sparse attention for long-context workloads.

people.names: Justin Dangel, Alexander Whedon, Ashley Miyasaki

innovation.assessment: The report describes a distinct sparse-attention design and long-context retrieval tests. Retrieving one planted fact and reliably reasoning across an entire long document are separate capabilities.
innovation.note: Standard attention can compare every token with every earlier token, making long inputs expensive. SubQ selects a subset of positions to attend to, then tests how much useful context it retains.

labs.name: Talkie
labs.focus: Trained a 13B language model on pre-1931 text to study knowledge and generalization.

team.people: Nick Levine, David Duvenaud, Alec Radford
team.background: The three researchers published the Talkie 13B historical language model.

people.names: Nick Levine, David Duvenaud, Alec Radford

innovation.assessment: The historical data cutoff creates a research instrument for testing what a model can infer without modern text. The main new contribution is the corpus and experimental setup, rather than the Transformer architecture.

labs.name: theyur (Dhamma Parrot)
labs.focus: Trained a small model in a personal pretraining experiment.
labs.size: Model card describes a personal project.

innovation.assessment: The open checkpoint documents a personal domain-specific pretraining run. It is primarily a reproducible example, with no general architecture gain established.

labs.name: Thinking Machines Lab
labs.focus: Develops Inkling models and studies reinforcement learning and post-training.

team.background: Team members have worked on ChatGPT, Character.AI, PyTorch, OpenAI Gym, and Segment Anything.

people.names: Mira Murati, John Schulman, Soumith Chintala

innovation.assessment: An agent uses Tinker to organize a fine-tuning run, load the new weights, and demonstrate a constrained writing task. This is a concrete integration of models and training tools. It does not establish open-ended self-improvement.
innovation.note: Tinker lets researchers run training updates and reuse the resulting checkpoint. The example explores how an agent could use that loop to adapt an existing model for a narrow writing task.

labs.name: Tilde Research
labs.focus: Studies new model architectures, pretraining, and interpretability.

team.background: The lab works on mechanistic interpretability, model architectures, and pretraining.

innovation.example: Sparse attention and controlled training experiments
innovation.assessment: The lab publishes experiments on reducing attention computation. The evidence is specific to the tested design. The savings and quality effects remain workload-dependent.

labs.name: TypeSafe AI
labs.focus: Trains Jev, a model for structured decisions in software.

people.names: Diogo Moitinho de Almeida, Erik Gafni, Sasha Sheng

innovation.assessment: Specializes for selecting from structured options rather than free-form generation. It demonstrates a narrower interface and workload. Claims of general efficiency need comparisons including constrained decoding.

labs.name: Tzafon
labs.focus: Trains computer-use models and released Northstar CUA research.

mentions.title: Tzafon nomination
mentions.author: jessicapeltz
mentions.note: A reply naming the computer-use model lab. The original chart had a higher valuation threshold.

innovation.assessment: Documents a specialized computer-use model with released research examples. The degree of advantage over prior UI control models depends on matched tasks and deployment setup.

labs.name: Unconventional AI
labs.focus: Researches computing with physical dynamics and trains experimental models on simulated substrates.

people.names: Naveen Rao, MeeLan Lee, Michael Carbin, Sara Achour

innovation.example: Un-0 image generation with coupled oscillators
innovation.assessment: The team demonstrates an image model using a simulated dynamical system. The experiments test the modeling approach. Energy and speed benefits on real hardware need separate measurement.
innovation.note: Un-0 generates a picture by simulating interacting oscillators. The team uses that experiment to study whether some model computation could eventually be performed by the dynamics of a physical circuit.

labs.name: VeroLM
labs.focus: Trains tiny byte-level language models from scratch.

innovation.assessment: Open byte-level pretraining provides a small test case for a known design family. Gains over equally sized subword models have not been established.

labs.name: WAR Enterprise
labs.focus: Trained a Portuguese-first small language model from scratch.
labs.size: Release post describes an independent developer.

team.background: Release post describes an independent developer.

innovation.assessment: Pretrained checkpoint adds a small Portuguese-first research baseline. Its evidence supports accessibility and domain coverage, rather than broader quality gains.

labs.name: Warp Sciences
labs.focus: Builds automated chemistry research infrastructure.

innovation.assessment: Public material describes the lab infrastructure. It leaves any separately attributable model contribution open.

labs.name: Wayve
labs.focus: Trains GAIA world models for closed-loop driving simulation and evaluation.

innovation.assessment: Lets the driving model interact with generated scenes instead of scoring only fixed clips. It makes evaluation more interactive. Simulation agreement with road outcomes still needs separate validation.

labs.name: World Labs
labs.focus: Trains spatial world models that generate navigable 3D scenes.

team.people: Fei-Fei Li, Justin Johnson, Ben Mildenhall, Christoph Lassner
team.background: The founding team works across computer vision, graphics, and generative AI.

people.names: Fei-Fei Li, Justin Johnson, Ben Mildenhall, Christoph Lassner

innovation.assessment: Marble makes generated scenes navigable and reusable as 3D assets. It applies existing spatial generation ideas in a working product. Real-world dynamics and long-horizon consistency are separate claims.
innovation.note: Marble generates a scene that users can move a camera through and export as 3D data. This makes it possible to inspect the same generated scene from several viewpoints.

labs.name: Xaira Therapeutics
labs.focus: Combines machine learning and experimental science for drug discovery.

people.names: Marc Tessier-Lavigne, David Baker, Arvind Rajpal, Vikram Bajaj, others

innovation.assessment: The corporate overview describes the research program. Its contribution to clinical outcomes requires evidence for specific candidates and studies.

labs.name: Zyphra
labs.focus: Develops Zamba hybrid state-space models, ZAYA reasoning models, and text diffusion models.

people.names: Krithik Puthalath, Danny Martinelli, Tomás Figliolia, Beren Millidge

innovation.assessment: Extends a state-space/attention hybrid to visual inputs. The work tests whether the language backbone’s latency advantages carry over to vision, building on prior state-space architectures.
